report.summary: Inventory-service p99 latency and errors jumped at 15:00 UTC, and checkout p99 followed (about 310ms to about 2.5s). The only change in the window is feature flag C09 at 14:55 UTC, which enabled realtime_stock_recalc for 100% of traffic (previously 5%). From 15:00 onward, inventory CPU went from about 30% to about 98% and the StockRecalculator.recomputeAll path ran over its 2000ms deadline on 48,211-SKU batches. The most likely cause is that the flag rollout saturated inventory-service CPU with full-catalogue recalculation. Health checks report green, which hides the problem. Request rate is flat, so this is not a traffic surge. Inventory-db shows only a modest CPU rise and no latency change, so the database is not the origin.

root_cause.mechanism: Feature flag realtime_stock_recalc was raised from 5% to 100% at 14:55Z. The full-catalogue StockRecalculator.recomputeAll (48,211 SKUs) then saturates inventory-service CPU, pushing requests past the 2000ms deadline, producing 9% errors, and driving checkout p99 to about 2.5s through sync HTTP calls.
assumptions: The flag is the only change in the window.
Health checks are shallow and don't exercise recalc.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: Increased query load from recalculation pushes inventory-db CPU up to about 60%, slowing inventory-service calls to the database.
assumptions: DB CPU rise is caused by recalc queries, which were not directly observed.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: Cache miss storms (57–80 misses/s) reduce cache hit rate, forcing recomputation on the database and CPU.
assumptions: The 14:09–14:19 storms are related to the 15:00 onset.

observed_facts.statement: Inventory-service cpu_pct rose from about 29.2–30.6% (14:00–14:55) to 98.43% at 15:00 and stayed 95–100% through 15:30.
Inventory-service error_rate rose from about 0.2% (14:00–14:55) to 9.33% at 15:00 and was 9.56% at 15:30.
A feature_flag change by p.nguyen at 14:55:00Z enabled realtime_stock_recalc for 100% of traffic, previously 5%.
From 15:00:06Z to 15:17:11Z, inventory-service logged repeated WARNs 'request exceeded deadline 2000ms in StockRecalculator.recomputeAll (sku_count=48211)', about one every 1–1.5 minutes.
Checkout-service latency_p99_ms rose from about 310–332ms (14:00–14:55) to 2512.95ms at 15:00 and 2666.13ms at 15:30; checkout error_rate and request_rate stayed flat.
Inventory-db query_latency_p99_ms stayed about 9ms and replication_lag_s about 0.3s throughout; db cpu_pct rose from about 30% to about 60–64% starting at 15:00.
Before onset, inventory-service logged cache miss storm warnings at 14:09:47, 14:11:57 and 14:19:19 (57–80 misses/s); no latency change followed in checkout.
Health checks at 15:28Z report inventory-service, inventory-cache, inventory-db and checkout-service healthy (HTTP 200 or SELECT 1).
Checkout-service logs show only one WARN in 14:50–15:30 (payment-service retry at 15:11:00).
The inventory-service metrics query returned partial data (2 of 5 series; memory, request_rate and latency_p99 missing).

assumptions: The realtime_stock_recalc flag is the only change affecting inventory-service in the window; change history covers 12:00–15:30 and shows only C09.
The 5-minute metric resolution means the flag change (14:55) and CPU onset (15:00) may differ by up to about 5 minutes; the exact onset is not resolved.
Health checks are shallow and do not exercise the recalculation path, so their green status does not rule out this fault.
Request rate for inventory-service is assumed flat because checkout request_rate is flat (inventory request_rate was not returned).

inferred_conclusions.statement: Enabling realtime_stock_recalc for 100% of traffic caused full-catalogue StockRecalculator work (48,211 SKUs per request) to saturate inventory-service CPU, causing deadline overruns, 9% errors and about 2.5s p99 latency.
Checkout latency is a downstream effect of the slow sync_http calls to inventory-service, not an independent fault; checkout itself shows normal CPU, memory and error rate.
Inventory-db is not the origin; its latency and replication stayed normal, and its CPU rise is consistent with the increased recalc query load.

remediation.action: Roll back or disable the realtime_stock_recalc feature flag, or set it back to 5% of traffic, to stop the recalculation load.
remediation.rationale: The flag change at 14:55 precedes the CPU and latency onset at 15:00, and the recalc deadline overruns follow it.

remediation.action: Verify that inventory-service CPU and p99 return to baseline (about 30% and under 300ms) and that checkout p99 recovers.
remediation.rationale: Confirms the mitigation and clears the P2 alert.

remediation.action: Make recalculation incremental or bounded by batch size instead of recomputing all 48k SKUs per request.
remediation.rationale: The sku_count=48211 full recompute is the expensive path.

remediation.action: Roll out feature flags progressively (5%→25%→100%) with CPU and latency guard checks.
remediation.rationale: A 5% to 100% jump in one step removed the safety margin.

remediation.action: Add a deep health check or SLO-based canary that exercises StockRecalculator.
remediation.rationale: Current health checks stayed green during the outage.

remediation.action: Review the cache miss storm alerting from 14:09–14:19 to see whether it is a separate issue.
remediation.rationale: It preceded onset but had no visible impact, so it is probably unrelated.

open_questions: Did the onset happen exactly at 14:55 (flag) or at 15:00? The 5-minute resolution cannot resolve this.
Why is inventory request_rate and latency_p99 not returned by the metrics shard (partial result)?
Does the cache miss storm at 14:09–14:19 share a cause with the recalc feature?
Was the 14:55 flag change applied to all inventory pods at once, or in a staged way?
